name: Ruslan Rahimkulov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Ruslan Rahimkulov and his older brother, Timur, became billionaires after inheriting the fortune from their father, Megdet, who led the Hungarian office of Russian gas giant Gazprom in the early 1990s.
Megdet Rahimkulov became CEO and co-owner of a joint venture between Gazprom and Hungary's oil and gas concern MOL in the mid 1990s.
The elder Rahimkulov also headed AEB, a Hungarian bank that Gazprom bought to process payments from its local customers that he later bought from Gazprom.
At the same time, he started began buying shares of MOL and OTP, Hungary's largest bank.
The brothers, both of whom live in Hungary, inherited the wealth in 2020 and began diversifying into other assets, including real estate.
forbes_facts: Megdet Rahimkulov was the richest person in Hungary before his return to Russia in 2008.

name: Stephane Bonvin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Stephane Bonvin is founder and CEO of Investis, a Swiss residential real estate firm, which he started in 1994.
Investis' portfolio consists of more than 3,000 apartments in the Lake Geneva region.
He took Investis public in 2016 on Swiss stock exchange SIX.
In 2006, Bonvin cofounded private equity firm Patrimonium, where he was managing director until 2015. In 2022, he sold his stake to his cofounders, citing an increased focus on Investis.

name: Jennifer Steinbrenner Swindal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Jennifer Steinbrenner Swindal is a general partner of the New York Yankees, the most valuable in baseball.
Her father, George, led a 12-person group of investors that bought the team from CBS for $10 million in 1973.
The Steinbrenner family also collectively owns more than 25% of YES Network, 20% of MLS's New York City FC, a stake in Legends Hospitality and 10% of Italian soccer club AC Milan.
George died in 2010, leaving an estimated one-fourth of his estate to each of Jennifer and her three siblings.
forbes_facts: George Steinbrenner died during a one-year repeal of the federal estate tax, saving his kids an estimated $600 million.

name: Nihat Ozdemir
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Nihat Ozdemir and his billionaire partner, Sezai Bacaksiz, met as students at Gazi University and founded Limak Construction in 1976.
Besides being contractor for some of the world's largest infrastructure projects, Limak has operations in energy, tourism, transportation and cement.
It's part of a consortium building Istanbul's new airport. When all phases are complete, it will be the world's largest based on passenger capacity.
Limak is a major builder and operator of hydroelectric power plants, ranking among Turkey's top ten electricity producers.
Besides Turkey, Limak operates in Kuwait, Egypt, Kosovo, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Eastern Europe, Africa, Pakistan, Ukraine and Russia.
forbes_facts: As an academic at what is now Gazi University, Ozdemir was for a short while assistant to Necmettin Erbakan, who went on to become minister of Turkey.
The future billionaire was on the faculty of the Engineering and Architecture department for four years, until 1980.

name: Fu Guangming
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026)
forbes_bio: Fu Guangming is the chairman of Fujian Sunner Development, which supplies chicken to KFC in China.
He shares his fortune with daughter Fu Fenfang, a company director, and his wife.
Fu is a member of China's Communist Party.

name: Charles Cohen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025)
forbes_bio: Real estate developer Charles Cohen bought out his father and uncle and quadrupled the family real estate empire to 12 million square feet.
Most of his fortune is in high end office buildings in New York City and design centers in several cities.
WeWork leases office space from Cohen Brothers Realty's 750 Lexington Avenue in Manhattan and the Pacific Design Center in Los Angeles.
Cohen owns high end luxury brands such as Harrys of London, Savile Row tailor Richard James and luggage company T. Anthony.
In 2018, he bought movie theater chain Landmark Theatres from Mark Cuban and picked up Manhattan society magazine Avenue.
He owns or has the rights to some 1,000 classic films.
forbes_facts: Cohen wrote the 1985 movie quiz book "Trivia Mania."
Cohen is buying and renovating historic movie theaters like Paris cinema La Pagode, the Larchmont Playhouse and the reopened Quad Cinema in Manhattan.
Cohen produced the 2008 Oscar-nominated "Frozen River" and distributed five foreign films nominated by the Academy Awards. He won for "The Salesman."

name: Winai Teawsomboonkij
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Winai Teawsomboonkij founded his Thaifoods Group in 1987 with a chicken farm of 20,000 chickens.
He went on to expand into breeding pigs and producing animal feed, taking the company public in 2015.
Winai holds a majority stake with his family in Thaifoods, one of the country's major chicken meat and pork producers.
The company also operates retail shops under the Thaifoods Fresh Market brand to sell food products with more than 600 outlets.
Winai resigned from CEO and director after Thai regulator imposed civil sanctions against him in late 2025 for insider trading.

name: Clelia Haji-Ioannou
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Clelia Haji-Ioannou is the daughter of Loucas Haji-Ioannou, the late Greek Cypriot shipping magnate (d. 2008).
She is a billionaire thanks to her stake in discount airline easyJet, founded by her brother Stelios.
She owns real estate across Europe, including properties in Monaco and Greece.
She also has a gallery outside of Athens featuring artwork by Picasso, Warhol and Dali.
forbes_facts: Haji-Ioannou oversaw the publication of a biography of her father, "Loucas Haji-Ioannou: The King of the Tankers."
Born in Athens, Clelia Haji-Ioannou holds both Cypriot and British citizenship and sits on the board of the Cyprus Marine Environment Protection Association.

name: Réal Plourde
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Réal Plourde is a cofounder and board member of Alimentation Couche-Tard, the Canadian convenience store giant that owns the Circle K chain.
Couche-Tard does $73 billion in annual revenue across more than 17,000 stores.
The chain has made three other cofounders billionaires: former CEO Alain Bouchard, Richard Fortin and Jacques D'Amours.
Couche-Tard has ballooned by snatching up competitors, including Minnesota-based Holiday Stationstores for $1.6 billion in 2017.
Plourde held a number of roles at the business, including chief operating officer and manager of technical services. From 2011 to 2014, he was chairman.

name: Vincent Lo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Vincent Lo is the chairman of Hong Kong-listed Shui On Land, best known for developing Shanghai's Xintiandi, an upscale shopping and entertainment district turned from a rundown area.
His daughter and heir apparent Stephanie is vice chairman of Shui On Land. Son Adrian is deputy CEO of Socam Development, the Hong Kong construction arm of Shui On.
Vincent is a son of late property tycoon Lo Ying-Shek, who cofounded Great Eagle Holdings. The clan has been embroiled in a feud over a family trust fund.
forbes_facts: Vincent Lo was sued by Donald Trump in 2005, who claimed former partners Lo and Henry Cheng had not consulted him and closed on a deal for less than he would have.
Trump lost the $1 billion case but was granted proceeds from another deal with the partners.

name: Henrik Fisker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021-2022)
forbes_bio: Henrik Fisker cofounded electric vehicle startup Fisker Inc., which  listed on the NYSE via a SPAC merger in 2020. He owns about 20% of the company.
An auto designer, he styled a BMW roadster for James Bond, luxury cars for Aston Martin and was a design consultant for Elon Musk's Tesla.
His first auto startup, Fisker Automotive, sold the luxury plug-in hybrid Karma; it filed for bankruptcy in 2014.
Fisker launched electric car startup Fisker Inc. in 2016 with his wife, Geeta Gupta-Fisker; she serves as Chief Financial Officer.
Its SUV is slated to begin production in late 2023 and will be built in the U.S. by Taiwan-based manufacturer Foxconn.
